extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors), editors, and reviewers interested in obtaining or providing PCI preprint recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria describing how the Peer Community In (PCI) recommendation process evaluates and handles preprints: who requests reviews, reviewer/editor selection and eligibility, transparency options, what is published, and what materials are reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation based on rigorous and transparent peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints are recommended by PCI on the basis of rigorous and transparent peer reviews; recommendation publicly guarantees scientific quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motivation of PCI is to establish a high-quality, free, public system for identifying high-quality preprints by a specific recommendation obtained after rigorous peer-review; the recommendation is intended to be recognized within and beyond the community (including by funding and research agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of eligible outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Only unpublished scientific papers deposited on open online archives (preprints) are the target outputs for PCI review and recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI handles articles not submitted to or published in journals and deposited on open archives like bioRxiv; recommended preprints become valid references and may be cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review requested by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors initiate the review request to a PCI community/editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review process is performed at the demand of the authors (authors request review of their preprints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are selected by the Editor, service, or community responsible for the PCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors select reviewers; reviewers may be chosen by the editor, the service, or the PCI community structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible reviewers/editors appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: New editors are nominated by a current editor of the PCI and must be approved by the Managing Board; reviewers are selected by editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial appointments follow nomination-and-approval by internal PCI governance; reviewer selection is the responsibility of editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage: complete paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are expected to cover the complete paper rather than a subsection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review policy indicates full-paper coverage is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may provide a response to reviews during the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author response is explicitly permitted (Author response: Yes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision format: binary
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decision on recommendation is binary (recommend or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review outcome is a binary decision, rather than a graded or multi-level verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identities are known to the editor or service (but not necessarily to authors or public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer identity known to: Editor or service; reviewers can choose anonymity for others (see anonymity options).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests checked
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests of participants are checked as part of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process includes checking competing interests (no further procedural detail given on page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial process publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial materials (reviews, editorial decisions, authors' replies) are published if the paper is accepted; nothing is published if the paper is rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accepted papers have their reviews and exchanges published; rejected submissions result in no public posting of the editorial record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity options for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may remain anonymous if they wish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system allows reviewers to be anonymous (reviewer anonymity is optional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity options for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can be anonymous to reviewers if they want to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author anonymity toward reviewers is optional and permitted by the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors must sign recommendation text upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is accepted/recommended, editors are required to sign the recommendation text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed editor recommendation provides accountability for acceptance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of code and data permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI explicitly reviews code and/or data associated with submitted preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of code or data: Yes — the process covers assessment of code and data where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI does not host the manuscript itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript hosting: No — PCI operates on preprints deposited in open archives rather than hosting files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interaction with the review process is not provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public interaction: No (the community does not provide an open public-commenting interface as part of the review process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for initial handling/inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one editor of the PCI must find the article interesting (for any reason: question, data, methods, results, discussion, etc.) to take it on for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An editor-level interest threshold is required before a submission will be evaluated; 'interesting' is interpreted broadly (any aspect of scientific interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency model options
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI supports multiple transparency models for peer review, including double blind, single blind, open identities, and open reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency options listed: Double blind, Open identities, Open reports, Single blind — the PCI can operate under different identity/reporting configurations depending on community/editor preferences.
